title: Great War of Saints and Demons

lines.en: Blue electricity sparked in the air, and the last charging android collapsed.
Pshhh.
Lee Jihye pulled her sword from the severed cables and wiped her forehead.
[Your level has increased!]
Watching beside her, Lee Gilyoung picked his nose and said,
“You're getting pretty good now, noona.”
At his sky-high arrogance, Lee Jihye nearly cracked him on the head, then stopped herself.
[You cannot attack the target.]
Those brats were invincible in this world anyway. Nothing good would come of upsetting them.
Lee Jihye looked between Lee Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung and asked,
“What levels are you two now?”
“What? You were 83 just a few days ago!”
“That was a lie, stupid.”
Watching the two children bicker, Lee Jihye answered with a sigh.

Still, the two children were helping her level up fast. She was leveling at the speed of light, as though they were literally power-leveling her, and it had earned them a place on Next City's wanted list.
[Android Lee Jihye — 1888G]
To be precise, only she had made the list. Since the children couldn't be attacked in the first place, they weren't even listed as wanted.
“I think it's about time we got out of this world.”
“I think it'll end if we bring that down.”

Shin Yoosung pointed to the enormous tower occupying the heart of Next City. A battleship floated above its summit, and whenever Lee Jihye looked at it, she received a message from her constellation sponsor.
[The constellation ‘Maritime War God’ insists that you must obtain that Star Relic.]
“······Well, this is a first. Our frugal general, of all people.”
[The constellation ‘Maritime War God’ clears his throat.]
Still, Lee Jihye could understand how her sponsor felt.
Anyone would probably understand once they saw that battleship.
“I don't know why something like that's here, but······.”
If she could take it with her, the skies of all these worlds would become the Maritime War God's sea.
Tightening her grip on her sword, Lee Jihye said,
“It'd be fun to give ajusshi and Master a surprise. Kids, shall we clear this now?”
“Sure. I was getting tired of using bugs anyway.”
“Let's do that.”
The unexpected message came just as the three, now of one mind, started toward the tower.
[An emergency patch has been applied!]
[As of midnight today, a shutdown system will be introduced to this scenario.]
[From now on, players under eighteen will be unable to use this scenario between midnight and 6 a.m.]
Lee Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung, who had been scampering along so cheerfully, staggered.
Lee Gilyoung murmured in confusion.
“Noona, I'm sleepy—”
“Unnie, run······!”
With those last words, the two children crumpled to the ground, asleep.
She held a hand beneath their noses and found they weren't dead.
[This player is currently shut down.]
Lee Jihye was dumbfounded.
“Wait, wasn't this world rated eighteen-plus to begin with? Why introduce a shutdown law?”
But she had no time to stand around complaining. The tower had opened wide, and hundreds of drones were launching at once to capture her.
It looked as though tonight would be a particularly long night.
[The 113th local battle has ended.]
[No winner or loser has been determined for this local battle.]

The war had neither victors nor vanquished. The gravely wounded demon kings withdrew, supporting one another, while the panicking Uriel was pushed away by lower angels. All that remained on the empty battlefield were reincarnators slumped like defeated soldiers, and five men and women sprawled among them.
“······I didn't think that would work.”
Han Sooyoung muttered in disbelief.
What <Kim Dokja's Company> had done in this local battle was simple.
Enter a battlefield of Good and Evil and subdue every participant except themselves.
Then keep the war going among those who remained, with neither side winning.
[The outcome of this battlefield cannot be determined.]
[The participants on this battlefield have been confirmed to have no intention of fighting.]

The contest between the members of <Kim Dokja's Company> had been play, sparring, a game without winners or losers, rather than a fight to the death. That made it no war of Good and Evil, and therefore no part of the Great War of Saints and Demons.
[This local battle has been removed from the classification ‘Great War of Saints and Demons’.]
[A new 113th local battle is awaiting creation.]
The military might to forcibly dismantle an entire battlefield.
That was the power <Kim Dokja's Company> now possessed.
“······My sponsor's going to be pretty hurt.”
“We had no choice this time, Heewon-ssi.”
“I'd rather not fight Uriel if I can help it.”
“Neither would I.”
With a faintly bitter expression, Jung Heewon joined Lee Hyunsung in checking on the reincarnators. Many had died and returned to the cycle of reincarnation, but some were still alive.

Jung Heewon and Lee Hyunsung divided up their [Ellain Forest's Vital Force] and shared it with them. Kim Dokja, too, helped the nearby reincarnators up one by one and stopped their bleeding with [Pressure Point].
Watching him, Han Sooyoung said,
“You did think this through before doing it this time, right?”
“I always think things through before doing them.”
“Then you know we can't hold out like this forever.”
They had timed their entry into the battlefield well this time, but there was no guarantee they would be so lucky again.

Among the constellations and demon kings belonging to Good or Evil, there were bound to be beings <Kim Dokja's Company> couldn't defeat on its own. They might leap into a battlefield with too great a gap in strength and find themselves in danger.
But Kim Dokja looked calm.
—It's fine. We don't need to hold out for long.
As they switched naturally to Midday Tryst, Han Sooyoung lowered her voice and asked,
—Then?
—We only need to hold out until the Chaos level passes 90.
[The current Chaos level is 56.]
Han Sooyoung scrutinized the message that appeared in the air as if it had been waiting.
—What's this number? It doesn't look like the Good and Evil levels.
—That's right.
Kim Dokja briefly explained the Chaos level.
When neither Good nor Evil won. When the order of this world broke down as a result—that was when this ‘Chaos level’ rose.
—What happens when it fills up?
—An apocalyptic calamity occurs.
—An apocalyptic calamity? ······Wait, you don't mean the ‘Apocalypse Dragon’?
The Ruin Dragon of the Book of Revelation, or the Final Dragon of the Book of Revelation.
The being commonly called the ‘Apocalypse Dragon’.
The great calamity that had returned in the 95th scenario of the 1863rd round and swept away the constellations of the <Star Stream> with a single swing of its tail.
Kim Dokja grinned and nodded.
—Right. You know your stuff.
—······You know that, and you're still going to raise the Chaos level? Are you insane? What'll you do if the Apocalypse Dragon revives? Have you forgotten what happened in the 1863rd round?
If the Apocalypse Dragon awoke in this scenario, it would bring destruction so great that the Great War of Saints and Demons itself would pale beside it.
But Kim Dokja's expression was firm.
—It won't revive.
—How do you know?
At Han Sooyoung's question, Kim Dokja merely shrugged and turned away. Just as the indignant Han Sooyoung was about to shout something, someone abruptly cut in.
“You call yourself an author, but you lack imagination.”
“What, you bastard?”
Yoo Joonghyuk easily caught Han Sooyoung's small fist.
Han Sooyoung growled.
“Why are you butting into someone else's conversation?”
“Your pathetic nonsense was more than I could bear.”
“What the hell are you talking about?”
“He isn't the only one who knows what happened in the 1863rd round.”
Han Sooyoung understood Yoo Joonghyuk at once.
Kim Dokja hadn't gone to the 1863rd round alone. He had left with two archangels, and one archangel had accompanied him back.
And what that meant was······.
“······Then <Eden> must know what happened there too. And he's using that.”
Kim Dokja's intent was clear.
When the Chaos gauge reached 100, the Apocalypse Dragon would be released.
And <Eden> had already heard about the 1863rd round and knew what would happen if the Apocalypse Dragon was released.
If they didn't want to see <Eden> destroyed, they had to stop the Great War of Saints and Demons right now.
That was the message Kim Dokja wanted to deliver.
Watching Kim Dokja reassure the reincarnators with perfect composure, Han Sooyoung felt a little dumbfounded.
Who else in the world would dare wage a campaign of threats against a great nebula?
“That wicked bastard······. He's telling them to choose: we all live, or we all die.”
“If it goes well. We may end up with a future where only we die.”
Wiping his [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] with a grim expression, Yoo Joonghyuk looked more serious than ever.
Han Sooyoung could read his resolve in that expression. Worst-case scenarios were probably running through his head one after another by now.
Kim Dokja's plan failing.
The companions of <Kim Dokja's Company> being wiped out here.
And him regressing once again.
Han Sooyoung grumbled.
“Is imagining nothing but horrible futures a regressor habit?”
“You must assume the worst to imagine what comes after it.”
“Anyone listening would think you'd regressed ten thousand times.”
“Perhaps I have, in some universe.”
“······I didn't know you could say things like that.”
Han Sooyoung gave a short laugh and looked at Kim Dokja in the distance.
Still looking sickly, he resembled a flailing inflatable tube man.
Just as she couldn't read the inside of that hollow figure, Han Sooyoung couldn't read Kim Dokja's mind.
Sometimes she felt as though she understood him, but it was usually no more than air leaking from the figure.
How she could trust someone like that.
Perhaps the one she truly couldn't understand was herself.
Why was she fighting alongside Kim Dokja?
She might find out if she ran [Predictive Plagiarism], but Han Sooyoung made no effort to do so.
Because she felt she shouldn't.
When she turned, Yoo Joonghyuk was watching the same scene.
“Hey, I've got a question.”
“It's remarkable that you imagine I would simply answer you.”
“Well, you are pretty tenacious. All that torture in the ‘Kaizenix Archipelago’, and you didn't let out a single groan.”
Yoo Joonghyuk's expression hardened.
“So you were behind that after all?”
“I didn't order anything. Our sweet Yuri just knew what I wanted.”
[The Story ‘King of Kaizenix’ nods.]
Even through Yuri's merciless torture, Yoo Joonghyuk hadn't revealed his identity or any related information. Han Sooyoung stood, dusting off her backside, and asked,
“Anyway, are you really okay now? You were trying to kill Kim Dokja before.”
“That is none of your business.”
“A guy like you wouldn't change his mind that quickly. And if your mind hasn't changed, that means you never intended to kill him in the first place······.”
“Who put you up to it back then? Metatron?”
At Metatron's name, Yoo Joonghyuk's thick brow shifted slightly.
“Hmm. So there does seem to be a connection.”
“······You've been digging into me?”
“When would I have time for that crap? You suddenly brought up <Eden>, so I was just fishing. ······But judging by your reaction, ‘Metatron’ doesn't seem to be the key.”
At Han Sooyoung's deduction, both of Yoo Joonghyuk's eyebrows twitched this time.
“Hmm, who could it be? Who got inside our precious regressor-nim's head?”
“He is not a being someone like you could know.”
“It's the ‘Secretive Plotter’, isn't it?”
Yoo Joonghyuk looked up at Han Sooyoung.
Han Sooyoung's lips twitched, as if asking why he was so surprised.
“I'm not an idiot, you know. I can think of anything you can.”
[The incarnation ‘Han Sooyoung’ is using ‘Predictive Plagiarism’.]
“More precisely, the ‘mes’ can.”
A Story in which hundreds, thousands, perhaps tens of thousands of Han Sooyoungs gathered to predict what would happen next.
This time, Yoo Joonghyuk asked,
“Do you know about the Secretive Plotter?”
“A very powerful Outer God.”
Yoo Joonghyuk looked disappointed for a moment, then spoke as though it made sense.
“······So gathering thousands of idiots doesn't make a genius.”
“Do you want to die? And do you know who he is?”
“There is someone I suspect.”
“Oh? Who?”
Rather than answering at once, Yoo Joonghyuk seemed to search his memory.
“······He knew my entire history. From the zeroth round to rounds in the distant future that I haven't experienced yet.”
“If my guess is right, there is only one such being across all these worldlines.”
Han Sooyoung nodded too.
“True. One possibility is more likely than all the others.”
They looked at each other for a moment, then gave their answers at the same time.
But.
“······Who did you say?”
“What nonsense is that?”
Their answers were different.
Han Sooyoung was the first to object.
“No, how could you even think that? Do regressors get stupider as they go?”
“I should be saying that. To think an author would put her imagination to such unpleasant use.”
Han Sooyoung and Yoo Joonghyuk glared at each other, growling.
Han Sooyoung was the first to give way.
“Phew······. I guess regressing three times could drive you crazy enough to think something weird. Fine······. You think the Secretive Plotter is ‘Kim Dokja from the future’?”
“That is what I believe.”
“Okay, well, it's not completely impossible. All kinds of things happen in the <Star Stream>, and besides······.”

Han Sooyoung was about to say, “This is a world where a novel became reality,” but swallowed the rest. Even if it was true, she felt it wasn't something to say in front of Yoo Joonghyuk. Instead, she said something else.
“The quickest way would be to ask the Secretive Plotter. Have you checked?”
Yoo Joonghyuk nodded.
“I made a contract with him. If I fulfilled his request, he would answer my questions.”
“What questions?”
“I asked whether the Secretive Plotter was Kim Dokja from the future.”
“And?”
“He said he wasn't.”
“Then why are you—”
“To be precise, he said, ‘I may have been something once, but now I am nothing.’”
He had been something once, but now he was nothing.
Han Sooyoung realized the loophole in those words.
The Secretive Plotter's answer didn't deny that he was ‘Kim Dokja from the future’. If anything, it was closer to saying he ‘might or might not have been Kim Dokja’.
Looking at it that way, she understood why Yoo Joonghyuk wouldn't abandon his deduction.
Han Sooyoung asked again.
“Is that all you heard?”
“He said he knew every round I have lived through.”
Someone who had once been something, but was now merely the ‘Secretive Plotter’.
And a being who knew every round Yoo Joonghyuk had lived through.
“Anything else?”
“No.”
“Are you kidding? You fought for your life, and that's all you asked?”
Han Sooyoung shouted, fuming.
“He wasn't there in your previous round, was he? If you couldn't get his exact identity, you should've gotten as much other information as possible!”
“······I did hear what he was after.”
“What did he say?”
“That there was something he wanted to change. And someone he wanted to kill.”
The more she heard, the deeper into a mire she felt herself sinking. ‘Someone he wanted to kill’ meant, in other words, ‘someone he couldn't kill yet’.
Could there be such a being, even for a god on the Secretive Plotter's level?
“That is everything I heard. And all the questions I was allowed.”
“Can't you dig up a little more information?”
“I would have to contract with him again. And if I did, I would pay a greater price than last time.”
Saying no more, Yoo Joonghyuk looked up into the air.
Han Sooyoung looked at the sky too. Then [Midday Tryst] activated.
—Is he watching?
—I sense no gaze.
It was a slightly disappointing result.
They had deliberately spoken out loud for him to hear, but it seemed the being in question wasn't watching. Rather unlike the ‘Secretive Plotter’, perhaps. Han Sooyoung said,
—That's a problem. If a god of that level interferes at a critical moment, it won't matter how carefully we plan.
Especially on a stage as important as this Great War of Saints and Demons. When one small variable could overturn the entire board, she couldn't help worrying.
But Yoo Joonghyuk thought differently.
“He won't act personally.”
“Why do you think that?”

“The fact that he works through Kim Dokja and me is proof. If he could act directly, he would have done so from the beginning. For a being of his level, acting personally would itself consume an enormous amount of probability.”
“······That's true. Never thought I'd find myself thanking that damned probability.”
“There is something I want to ask, too.”
“Hm?”
“I have yet to hear the basis of your unpleasant imagining. Why do you think the ‘Secretive Plotter’ is ‘that person’······?”
Han Sooyoung gave a short laugh at his question.
“What, I thought you weren't interested. Does it bother you?”
“You never miss a chance to talk back.”
Just as Yoo Joonghyuk was about to grip his cold sword hilt, a sly voice reached them.
“You two get along well.”
Their murderous gazes landed on Kim Dokja at the same time.
As Kim Dokja retreated, waving his hands with a wry smile, a scenario message appeared in the air.
[New coordinates have been set for the 113th local battle.]
The companions' gazes settled on Kim Dokja.
At last, it was time to move again.
“Let's go another round.”
As though they had been waiting, the Stories of <Kim Dokja's Company> began clamoring.
[A new Story is budding within the demon king ‘Demon King of Salvation’!]
[A list of candidates for the second modifier of the ‘Demon King of Salvation’ has been generated.]
The Demon Realm's second-in-command was known by many modifiers.
Ruler of Eastern Hell. Deputy of the Demon Realm (代手). Destroyer of Dignity.
For all those names, he had only one true name.
Agares, master of the Second Demon Realm.

Ever since the master of the First Demon Realm had abruptly vanished, Agares had guarded the Demon Realm for thousands of years. He had beheaded archangels who coveted his territory and protected the Stories that allowed Evil to exist as Evil.
Testing the qualifications of Evil, regulating and ruling it, he had immersed himself in a single question.
For what purpose did Evil exist?
Whenever he tore a life apart, he immersed himself in that question. Whether it could truly be answered didn't matter. The question itself kept him alive.
[The 113th local battle has been forcibly terminated.]
[The 114th local battle has been forcibly terminated.]
Yet even after living for so many ages, he had never seen anything like this.
—Hold on just a little longer, everyone!
—We've almost subdued them all!
There were people rescuing reincarnators from the hellish battlefield.
Regardless of the outcome of that great contest of Good and Evil, someone was saving the expendable lives sacrificed there.
Ordinarily, it would have been an act of [Good].
The problem was that the being doing it was a [Demon King].
[The Chaos level has increased by 4.]
[The current Chaos level is 60.]
[Warning! The Chaos level has exceeded 60!]
Chaos.
Neither Good nor Evil.
Something outside the world's probability and order.
[He means to stop the Great War of Saints and Demons by raising the Chaos level?]
Red horns grew through the fedora Agares wore pulled low. It was a trait that appeared whenever something interested him.
[Preventing a smaller destruction by threatening a greater one. Just the sort of idea the Demon King of Salvation would have.]
The speaker was Asmodeus, the ‘Devil of Lust and Wrath’.
Agares twitched a finger resting on his throne and asked,
[Why does he not side with ‘Evil’? He would lose nothing by joining us.]
[When this Great War of Saints and Demons ends, his ‘Climax (轉)’ will be complete. It must mean the ■■ he seeks is not the path of Evil.]
[Yet he does not seem to seek the ■■ of Good, either.]
If anything, it was more troublesome than if he had taken either side.
Agares asked again.
[What do you think?]
[Metatron will move before we do. That old angel has longed for this war longer than anyone. He won't stand by and watch his game be ruined.]
No sooner had he spoken than a message arrived through the demon kings' communications.
—Agares. I contacted you because there is something I must tell you.
Agares smiled, the corners of his torn mouth lifting.
—Metatron. We are hardly on terms for a leisurely conversation.
The strongest beings of the present Demon Realm and Eden faced one another through a screen. Their exchanged gazes alone sent powerful sparks of probability flying.
—I'd like to play along, but this time I believe I need to borrow your strength for a moment.
—Have you ever heard a story of Good and Evil joining hands?
—Stories of Evil pursuing its ends by any means are quite common.
Metatron remained calm in the face of Agares's mockery.
—There is a childish nebula. Young newcomers who believe themselves the center of this world.
It was obvious whom he meant. Agares laughed.
—Opening a hotline just to trample one tiny nebula? How amusing.
—If we aren't careful, one tiny nebula may bring down the Great War of Saints and Demons.
—So, as their senior in the <Star Stream>, you want to discipline them? Still the same overbearing old man.
—Let us say I wish to teach them the true workings of the world.
—I refuse. Crushing a nebula like that is nothing, even without joining hands with you.
—I'm not asking to join hands.
—Then?
Instead of answering at once, Metatron floated a small cross above his hand. Suspended in the air, the cross spun in place.
—<Kim Dokja's Company> can ruin the battlefields because they exploit an even balance of power.
—And?
—But what if the balance of power is broken from the outset?
Metatron blew on the cross. Its axis of rotation tilted slightly, and it began to wobble. Agares asked in displeasure,
—You mean to open a battlefield where one side is at a disadvantage from the start?
—Exactly.

With evenly matched forces, it would be one thing. But if the balance tipped to one side, <Kim Dokja's Company> would have to supply the weight to restore it. If it tipped toward Evil, they would have to add their weight to Good; if toward Good, to Evil.
If they turned this against the Company, it would not be impossible to design a local battle that would wipe out <Kim Dokja's Company>.
—Which side do you propose putting at a disadvantage?
—We should be fair in these matters. For every local battlefield we open that disadvantages Evil, we will open one that disadvantages Good.
—Interesting. You want to catch them even at the cost of sacrificing angels?
—We cannot allow the Chaos level to keep rising. And opening several local battles will let us divide <Kim Dokja's Company>.
—What if they don't respond to the provocation?
—Would that not be enough in itself?
Metatron's eyes shone white on the other side of the screen.
—If they refuse, Good and Evil (善惡) will win this war anyway.
[The gate to local battle 115 has opened!]
[The gate to local battle 116 has opened!]
[The gate to local battle 117 has······!]
Watching gates fill the air in real time, I gave a hollow laugh.
Of course Metatron and Agares wouldn't just let this go.
Watching the portals appear and disappear in real time, Jung Heewon asked,
“Dokja-ssi, what's going on?”
“They've opened the local battles all at once.”
“Can that happen?”
“Normally, no. Even local battles don't appear and disappear that quickly.”
[Local battle 115 has ended!]
[Local battle 116 has ended!]
As battlefields closed in real time, scenario messages appeared as well.
[Great War of Saints and Demons — Progress]
Absolute Good level: 57
Absolute Evil level: 57
Chaos level: 60
As though countering the Chaos level we had built up, the Good and Evil levels were rising fast. Lee Hyunsung was the one who finally sprang up.
“We can't just stay here.”
Clenching his fists, he continued.
“There must be reincarnators being sacrificed on those battlefields too.”
“Of course there are. But if we go in, we'll die too.”
Han Sooyoung spoke, chewing at a fingernail.
“Don't you get it? It's a trap. They've teamed up to kick our asses.”
At Lee Hyunsung's blank look, I nodded.
“Han Sooyoung is right. We'll probably be attacked the moment we enter.”
“We are finished even if we do not enter.”
At Yoo Joonghyuk's words, the companions' expressions darkened further.
<Kim Dokja's Company> was split between Good and Evil.

If the Great War of Saints and Demons ended like this, whichever side lost would meet a terrible fate. Their incarnation bodies would naturally be destroyed, and even if they were lucky enough to become souls, the fires of Hell would torment them until their sense of self was destroyed.
In the end, we had no choice but to enter those battlefields.
“······We have no choice, then.”
Sometimes you had to walk into a trap even knowing what it was.
I quickly divided up the companions.
“Jung Heewon-ssi and Lee Hyunsung-ssi, enter local battle 117. Han Sooyoung and Yoo Joonghyuk, take gate 119—”
“No, wait. What about you?”
“I'll take gate 121 alone.”
Yoo Joonghyuk glared at me and silently gripped his sword hilt, so I hurried to protest.
“No, I don't mean I'm really going alone.”
“Who are you going with?”
“Someone who'll be on our side.”
Han Sooyoung objected.
“Who? Who's going to take our side now?”
Ordinarily, no one would.
But if I was right, at least one. No, two.
[The nebula <Underworld> is waiting for you.]
I grinned and said,
“My parents.”
After a brief goodbye to the companions, I immediately sent a message to the <Underworld>. The reply came quickly.
[The constellation ‘Father of the Rich Night’ grants you permission to enter.]
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ grants you permission to enter.]
[The nebula <Underworld> opens a portal to summon you.]
Tzzzzzt!
Normally, leaving a large-scale scenario in progress wasn't easy. But the <Underworld> had willingly paid an enormous amount of probability for me.
I was grateful.
I was supposed to be their heir, but I hadn't even properly paid my respects since they'd helped me back then······.
Come to think of it, I felt a little uneasy. What if they had agreed so readily because they wanted to thrash me for never visiting the <Underworld>?
—Kim Dokja.
Startled by the sudden message, I looked into the air. It wasn't [Midday Tryst]. That left only one person who would send me a message.
—What is it? I thought becoming a branch chief kept you busy. You still have time to worry about this place?
—I don't. I make time.

Bihyung grumbled in midair, a tobacco leaf between his lips. The guy seemed pretty worn out from work lately, now that he'd become a branch chief. He looked down at me with a conflicted expression and sighed deeply. Then I felt transmission and reception on the nearby channels temporarily cut off.
—You're doing something dangerous.
—When haven't I?
—It's different this time. The entire <Star Stream> is watching what you're doing.
—I feel like I've heard that more than a hundred times too.
—At this rate, the karma of the probability you've built up will explode soon. You know what that means?
I nodded. I had seen exactly what horrors an explosion of distorted probability could cause during the ‘Demon King Selection’.
In fact, lately I often felt like I was standing atop a Jenga tower with too many blocks missing.
—Be careful. Your luck can't last forever. Even if you have the protection of great dokkaebis and Outer Gods······.
—Whose protection?
—······Forget it. I said something unnecessary.
Bihyung shook his head and blew a little smoke into the air. Around the smoke, the frozen channels began to resume.
—Have a good trip. Don't die.
—Is that what you say to someone going to the afterlife?

He didn't say so, but Bihyung was probably blocking interference from the Bureau. He had been a low-ranking dokkaebi when we first met, and now he was helping me this much. Live long enough, and you see all sorts of things.
[Spacetime transfer begins.]

The sensory information before me broke apart. When I opened my eyes again, the black, parched earth of the afterlife greeted me. The <Underworld>. Normally I would have to cross the river with the ferryman Charon, but that procedure had been omitted this time.
How long had I walked past the dry riverbank's gravel beds toward Hades's palace?
The moment I stepped into the outer fortress, tens of thousands of gazes fixed on me as though they had been waiting.
An enormous number of souls, headed by the three great judges of the afterlife. Judging by the fierce movement of the air, their gazes seemed far from friendly.
[The judges of the afterlife have noticed your presence!]
So they really had called me here for another reason?
Ssshh.
Giving off a Status that seemed ready to mummify every living thing, the three great judges glided toward me.
All three judges were Narrative-grade constellations.
I quickly gripped [Unbreakable Faith] at my waist.
However much stronger I had become, facing them in the <Underworld> would be no easy task.
That was when the eye level of the judge at the front began to drop.
Then the second judge's eye level dropped, followed by the third's. The judges were kneeling before me.

Behind them, the army of the <Underworld> began sinking to the ground like a low, surging wave. Looking more closely, I realized that the fiercely seething heat was rather different from what I had imagined. The judges of the afterlife dabbed at their eyes as they looked at me. As though something had moved them.
Ruuumble!
The entire <Underworld> was kneeling before me, opening a path.
A path to the palace's inner chambers.
A path that, until now, only two constellations had been permitted to walk.
[Welcome to the Kingdom of Night, heir to the <Underworld>!]
Along with the judge's words, a system message appeared before me.
[You are currently the prince of the <Underworld>.]
I felt uneasy all the way into the palace.
The moment I became ‘heir to the Underworld’, I had thought something like this might happen. Still, experiencing such a steep rise in status left my mind feeling like mush.
I had never been treated so lavishly in my life.
